To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SLAC polarised photoabsorbtion data can be described with a simple Regge model and that this data gives a first estimate of 0.5 for the high-energy part (x > 0.3) of the Drell Hearn Gerasimov sum rule for the proton.

(i) the SLAC data is in good agreement with our Regge model, (ii) our model gives a first estimate of 0.5 +/- 0.2 of the Drell- Hearn-Gerasimou sum-rule and (iii) the data is consistent with the predictions of the Ellis-Jaffe sum-rule.

(a) the spin dependence of high energy photoabsorption is not understood; (b) the spin dependence is not a simple function of the photon helicity; (c) there are large differences in the spin dependence between the u and d quarks; (d) there is evidence for the presence of a large gluon contribution to the spin of the proton.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of high-energy photo-absorption in the low x region.
a number of aspects of the polarised structure of the nucleon, and in particular with the role of the spin dependent Regge trajectories.
the spin and flavour dependence at large x, and the spin dependence at low x, of photoabsorption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we do not know what we are talking about.
the spin dependent Regge model is not yet able to describe the data in all details.
the data are not yet good enough to make a definitive statement about the validity of the sum-rule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present data is not yet precise enough to allow a reliable determination of the high-energy contribution to the Drell-Hearm-Gerasimov integral.
the spin dependent part of the Regge theory is in a good agreement with the data.
the data are consistent with the spin-flavour symmetry and the predictions of the spin-flavour Reggeon field theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high-energy part is not negligible and is likely to be negative.
the spin dependent data can only be explained by a large contribution from the pomeron.
the spin and flavour dependence is very different from what is expected from Regge theory.
